interest: Shows wartime FBI monitoring of suspected Japanese agents in Colombia, whom Colombian authorities declined to intern for lack of evidence.
overview: This file, classified under State Department decimal file 894.20221 (Military Activities of Japan in Colombia: Espionage and Propaganda), concerns U.S. and Colombian intelligence investigations into Hesagoshi Eshima Yasumaga, a Japanese national resident in Bogotá during World War II. It centers on a February 1945 communication from FBI Director J. Edgar Hoover to Frederick B. Lyon at the Department of State, forwarding a January 1945 investigative report on Yasumaga. The report details allegations that Yasumaga, a former clerk and translator at the Japanese Legation in Bogotá, was gathering intelligence for the Spanish Legation and was employed as an instructor at La Escuela Normal Superior. Evidence submitted to the Colombian National Police for his internment or deportation was reviewed in late 1944 and judged insufficient by Colombian authorities. The remainder of the file contains National Archives withdrawal sheets for restricted and security-classified items, including a December 1945 document between Keown and Lynn.
